# Intake Brief: Audit freshness invalidates only on this work item's own data change

## Problem statement

The audit freshness gate (`_check_audit_freshness` / `_compute_content_fingerprint`
in `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`) invalidates a stored audit when any
fingerprint component changes. The original formulation fingerprinted
**whole-repo** state (git HEAD sha + work-item description hash + Key Files +
whole-repo working-tree hash), so any commit or uncommitted/untracked change
anywhere in the repository — even one from an *unrelated* work item — invalidated
every stored audit and re-triggered the full audit pipeline.

**Observed failure (SA-0MSN04X2S006ONH0):** audited "Ready to close: Yes" at HEAD
`310773d5`; afterwards an unrelated work item (SA-0MSQ026T3009QY2L) merged
`aaabdede` to dev, the fingerprint changed (`58947e06…` matched recomputation at
`310773d5` but not at `aaabdede`), the re-audit ran and blocked on the pre-flight
full-suite cache gate — a verified item stuck in review.

**Current state (2026-10-21, HEAD `fe85415a3`):** the whole-repo components have
**already been replaced** by per-touched-file scoping (SA-0MSPZDALB000S18P, done):
the payload is now `{path_states, description_hash, key_files}` where each
touched path contributes its committed state (blob hash at HEAD, else the latest
touching commit) plus its narrowed working-tree state. An unrelated commit or
working-tree change now invalidates **only if it touches a file in the item's
touched set** (commits referencing the item id + comment-recorded commit hashes +
Key Files). The whole-repo HEAD sha is no longer a component, and
`_resolve_working_tree_hash` no longer exists. The observed failure case is
therefore **no longer reproducible** with today's formula.

The remaining delta of this item is the **strict rule** recorded in the original
Q&A: "An audit is only invalidated if there is a change to this work item's data
AFTER the audit was created." That rule is stronger than the current
per-touched-file formula — it requires a fingerprint over the item's own data
only (title + description, which contains the ACs and Key Files), with **zero git
calls**, so even a committed/uncommitted change to a file this item touched does
not invalidate.

## Users

- Audit operators / automated dispatchers relying on `audit_runner.py` freshness
  short-circuit (SA-0MSKB6US1009CNHT) to skip re-audits of unchanged items.

**User story:** "As an audit operator, I want a stored audit to remain valid
unless THIS work item's own data changes, so unrelated repository activity
(including changes to files this item happened to touch) doesn't invalidate my
audits."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `_compute_content_fingerprint` is computed from the **work item's own data
   only** — the item's title + description (the description contains the ACs and
   the Key Files section, so `key_files` may remain in the payload as a
   deterministic derivative of it). The per-path git components (committed HEAD
   blob hashes, working-tree state) and the whole-repo HEAD component are
   **removed** from the fingerprint — **no git calls in the computation**
   (`_resolve_touched_files` / `_compute_path_fingerprints` are no longer used by
   the fingerprint). *(Producer decision 2026-10-21: proceed with the strict
   formula — recorded below.)*
2. A git HEAD move caused by ANY other work item's commit does **not** invalidate
   a stored audit of an item whose own data is unchanged. Regression test:
   fingerprint is stable when only the HEAD sha differs (item data identical).
3. Uncommitted and untracked working-tree changes do **not** invalidate a stored
   audit — **including changes to files the item itself touched** (stricter than
   the current per-touched-path formula). Regression test: fingerprint is stable
   across `git status --porcelain` / `git diff --name-only HEAD` differences and
   across touched-file edits.
4. A change to this item's own data (title / description / ACs / Key Files
   section) after the audit **does** invalidate and re-runs the pipeline (existing
   description/key-files fingerprint tests remain green).
5. Comments, status/stage/priority/assignee changes, and sortIndex changes do
   **not** invalidate (they move `updatedAt` but are not audited content). This
   also removes the current comment-recorded-commit-hash contribution to the
   touched set (SA-0MVAWFYKT002CQ3L) — the fingerprint must not depend on comments.
6. **Migration of legacy reports:** reports persisted before this change carry
   fingerprints computed with the git-inclusive formulas that cannot be recomputed.
   Version the fingerprint line (e.g. `Audit content fingerprint (v2): <hash>`)
   so legacy/unversioned lines are distinguishable; legacy/unversioned reports
   fall back to the existing time-gate floor (auditedAt vs updatedAt +
   `AUDIT_FRESHNESS_BUFFER_SECONDS`, plus the persist-write tolerance) — **no
   silent mass re-audit wave** of the existing in_review backlog. Document the
   one-time re-audit consequence for legacy items whose `updatedAt` moved after
   the audit, and its interaction with the pre-flight full-suite cache gate.
7. Dead code cleanup: after the simplification, remove the fingerprints-only
   git machinery no longer referenced elsewhere (verify each of
   `_resolve_touched_files` / `_compute_path_fingerprints` — those still used by
   the file-scope manifest and Phase 2 remain). `_resolve_working_tree_hash`
   (SA-0MSL1YXG7004F2BZ) is **already removed**; `_resolve_audited_head` stays
   (still used by green-run attestation).
8. **Test migration (nothing silently dropped):** the existing per-touched-path
   invalidation tests (`test_fingerprint_changes_when_touched_file_committed_change`,
   `..._dirty`, `..._staged`, `test_tool_artefact_rewrite_invalidates`, the
   comment-contribution tests, `test_unrelated_commit_does_not_reauth`) are
   rewritten to assert the **new rule** rather than deleted; new/updated tests
   cover title-change invalidation, stability across touched-file edits, and the
   versioned-line legacy fallback to the time gate.
9. Documentation updated: `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` (freshness-gate
   section, currently ~lines 248-318/579-594/699/816), `skill/audit/SKILL.md`
   (~lines 42/182-186/204-210), and the code docstrings on
   `_check_audit_freshness` / `_compute_content_fingerprint` /
   `AUDIT_CONTENT_FINGERPRINT_PREFIX`. All fingerprint call sites that must keep
   working with the simplified formula: `_check_audit_freshness` (item gate),
   `_get_child_audit_verdict` + `_child_content_changed` (child reuse, LP-0MSQ32MF200675AR),
   `cmd_check_freshness` (read-only probe, SA-0MUOO5W8J001DYTI),
   `_run_remediation_loop` (ruff-config re-hash), `_phase_fetch_and_cq`,
   `_reaudit_budget_exceeded_children`, `_phase_children` (child audit persistence).
   **All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes** — code
   comments/docstrings, README, and any wiki or docs-site entries that describe
   the freshness gate. Full project test suite passes with the changes.

## Constraints

- **Verdict semantics unchanged:** the rule is about *when an existing audit is
  reused*, never about what the audit concludes. `--force` still bypasses the
  gate.
- **Read-only:** the fingerprint change must not execute the test suite or make
  any pi calls.
- **No regression in the freshness skip:** items whose data is unchanged still
  short-circuit in seconds (SA-0MSKB6US1009CNHT intent preserved); the read-only
  `check-freshness` probe and `isAuditFresh` (ship, SA-0MUOO5W8J001DYTI) keep
  working.
- **Fail-open preserved:** any failure to compute the new fingerprint still falls
  through to a full re-audit (existing behaviour).
- **Child reuse gate:** child-audit reuse uses the same fingerprint — it must keep
  working with the simplified formula (children's own data unchanged → reused).

## Existing state

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`:
  - `_compute_content_fingerprint` (line ~2412) — payload =
    `{path_states, description_hash, key_files}` (per-touched-path, SA-0MSPZDALB000S18P).
  - `_check_audit_freshness` (line ~1950) — content gate primary; time gate
    (60 s + persist-write tolerance ~30 s) floor for fingerprint-less legacy
    reports; persistence-write tolerance covers the runner's own writes
    (SA-0MTHC710X003ORZM).
  - `_extract_content_fingerprint` (line ~2073) — parses the unversioned line.
  - `_resolve_touched_files` (line ~2213), `_compute_path_fingerprints`
    (line ~2336) — the per-touched-path git machinery this item's strict rule
    removes from the fingerprint (verify remaining uses: file-scope manifest at
    ~5224/7964/10897).
  - `AUDIT_CONTENT_FINGERPRINT_PREFIX = "Audit content fingerprint: "` (line ~1112,
    unversioned); embedded at ~5721/5747/6172 (persist) + re-extracted by the gate.
  - Call sites of the fingerprint: `_check_audit_freshness` (~2020),
    `_get_child_audit_verdict` (~6606), `_child_content_changed` (~7009),
    `cmd_check_freshness` (~2117/2120), `_phase_gate` (~9466),
    `_run_remediation_loop` (~10171), `_phase_fetch_and_cq` (~10357),
    `_reaudit_budget_exceeded_children` (~10786), `_phase_children` (~11380/11516/11918).
  - `_resolve_working_tree_hash` — **already removed** (SA-0MSL1YXG7004F2BZ
    component replaced by per-path state); `_resolve_audited_head` (~2852) stays.
- `skill/audit/tests/` — tests split across files; fingerprint/freshness coverage
  lives mainly in `test_audit_runner_freshness.py` (1336 lines:
  `TestTouchedFileResolution` ~190, `TestContentFreshnessGate` ~348 — incl.
  `test_fingerprint_payload_keys_exclude_global_head`, touched-file invalidation
  tests, `test_unrelated_commit_does_not_reauth`, comment-hash tests) and
  `test_audit_runner_check_freshness.py`. Some existing tests assert the
  per-touched-path invalidation behaviour that this item reverses
  (`test_fingerprint_changes_when_touched_file_committed_change` /
  `..._dirty` / `..._staged`, tool-artefact invalidation, comment-contribution
  tests, `test_child_content_changed_fresh_survives_unrelated_head_movement` —
  these must be updated to the new rule).
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — freshness-gate section ~lines 248-254
  (content gate + time gate + fail-open), 292/309-318 (child reuse), 579/594
  (inherited pass / child reuse), 699/816 (Phase 2 child reuse).
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — freshness-gate summary ~lines 42, 182-186, 204-210.
- Related (separate repo, out of scope): herdr downtime worker's dispatcher-side
  `isAuditFresh` (ContextHub `packages/herdr/src/icons.ts`, time-based
  `auditedAt > updatedAt - 60s`) caused the re-dispatch that exposed this;
  covered by RCA WL-0MSRBFFLN005W3VT (ContextHub worklog). The ship-side
  `isAuditFresh` consumption is SA-0MUOO5W8J001DYTI (done) and stays in scope
  only as a consumer that must keep working.

## Desired change

Change `_compute_content_fingerprint` to hash only the work item's own data —
`{title, description_hash}` (Key Files parse from the description; explicitly
admit `key_files` in the payload or rely on `description_hash` as the ACs allow)
— with a versioned fingerprint line so legacy unversioned reports fall back to
the time-gate floor. Remove the per-path git components and the now-unused git
machinery from the fingerprint path; keep `_resolve_audited_head` for green-run
attestation; keep every consumer (item gate, child reuse, read-only probe,
remediation re-hash, child persistence) working against the simplified formula.
Update the fingerprint/freshness tests and both docs files to the new rule.

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_compute_content_fingerprint`
  (simplify to item-data-only), `_check_audit_freshness` / `_extract_content_fingerprint`
  (versioned-line handling), `AUDIT_CONTENT_FINGERPRINT_PREFIX`, dead-git-
  machinery removal, docstrings
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_freshness.py` and
  `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_check_freshness.py` — update
  fingerprint/freshness tests to the new rule
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — freshness-gate section
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — freshness-gate summary lines

## Related work

- `SA-0MSPZDALB000S18P` — Audit freshness: re-audit only when files touched by
  the work item changed (**done**, 2026-09-28) — implemented the per-touched-path
  formula currently in the code; this item's strict rule goes further (item-data-
  only, zero git). **The original observed failure is already fixed by this item.**
- `SA-0MSL1YXG7004F2BZ` — Include working-tree state in the audit content
  fingerprint (**done**, not in_review as the original brief stated) — the
  whole-repo working-tree component this item's rule REMOVES (superseded; the
  per-path state it inspired is also removed by this strict rule).
- `SA-0MSKB6US1009CNHT` — Audit: content-based freshness gate (**done**) —
  introduced the fingerprint; this item simplifies its scope.
- `SA-0MVAWFYKT002CQ3L` — Stabilise child freshness fingerprint comments
  (**done**, 2026-10-21) — comment-recorded commit hashes feed the touched set;
  this item's rule removes the comment dependency (AC5).
- `SA-0MUOO5W8J001DYTI` — Ship: consume persisted audit content fingerprint
  (**done**) — read-only `check-freshness` probe consumer that must keep working.
- `SA-0MSN04X2S006ONH0` — Audit runner: detect proxy 'cheap' mode (**done**) —
  the item whose blocked re-audit exposed this problem.
- `WL-0MSRBFFLN005W3VT` — RCA: Downtime dispatcher re-dispatches same item
  (ContextHub worklog) — dispatcher-side re-dispatch trigger; separate concern,
  out of scope.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption — "this work item's data":** title + description (ACs + Key Files
  section). Comments, lifecycle fields, and repo state are NOT audited content
  and must not invalidate.
- **Assumption — migration via versioned line:** legacy/unversioned reports fall
  back to the time gate (existing floor for fingerprint-less reports). A legacy
  item whose `updatedAt` moved after its audit is re-audited once, then stores a
  v2 fingerprint and is immune to comment/HEAD/working-tree churn thereafter.
  Accepted: this is a one-time, bounded transition.
- **Risk — stale code evidence (now broader):** dropping the per-path git
  components means a stored audit may reference code that changed under it — not
  just via another work item's Key-File edit, but **any committed or uncommitted
  change to a file this item touched** (the protection deliberately added by
  SA-0MSL1YXG7004F2BZ and kept by SA-0MSPZDALB000S18P, with tests asserting the
  invalidation). Accepted by design — producer confirmed option (a) on
  2026-10-21 (comment SA-C0MVIAGIQU003WW4P); the audit's verdict remains the
  record for the item's own data.
- **Scope-creep risk:** reversing the per-touched-path design re-touches the
  child-reuse gate, the read-only probe, and the ship-side `isAuditFresh`
  consumer. Keep those as consumers that must keep working — do not extend the
  item to re-design them.
- **Risk — herdr re-dispatch noise:** herdr may still dispatch /skill:audit for
  items whose `updatedAt` moved; with this fix the runner short-circuits
  ("Skipping: audit still fresh", zero pi calls). Dispatcher-side change is out
  of scope (RCA WL-0MSRBFFLN005W3VT).

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q: Should a git HEAD move from another work item invalidate this item's audit?
  — Answer (user): No. "An audit is only invalidated if there is a change to
  this work item's data AFTER the audit was created." The rule is that simple.
- Q: What about the working-tree component (SA-0MSL1YXG7004F2BZ)? — Answer:
  remove it too — same reasoning (repo state, not item data). This item
  supersedes SA-0MSL1YXG7004F2BZ's component.
- Q: Do comments / status / stage changes invalidate? — Answer (assumed, per
  rule): no — they are not this item's audited data. Document as an explicit
  decision.
- Q: Migration of existing stored fingerprints? — Answer (assumed): version the
  fingerprint line so legacy reports are distinguishable; legacy → existing
  time-gate floor; no mass re-audit wave.

- Q (scope decision, 2026-10-21): The original trigger (unrelated whole-repo
  churn invalidating audits) was already fixed by SA-0MSPZDALB000S18P, so the
  strict item-data-only rule additionally removes per-touched-file protection
  (committed/uncommitted changes to files the item touched no longer
  invalidate), reversing tested behaviour shipped in SA-0MSPZDALB000S18P /
  SA-0MSL1YXG7004F2BZ. — Answer (Map, on behalf of producer): "a" — proceed
  with the strict item-data-only formula (title + description only, zero git
  calls), as originally recorded; per-touched-path invalidation tests are
  rewritten to the new rule. Source: comment SA-C0MVIAGIQU003WW4P (reply to
  comment SA-C0MVI9Q5L3008NBLW). Research: inspected
  `_compute_content_fingerprint`/`_check_audit_freshness`/
  `_extract_content_fingerprint` at HEAD `fe85415a3`; confirmed whole-repo HEAD
  and `_resolve_working_tree_hash` are gone and the payload is
  `{path_states, description_hash, key_files}`; confirmed per-touched-path
  invalidation tests exist in `test_audit_runner_freshness.py`.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MVAWFJXM0096FAB** – Child freshness fingerprint test coverage (completed)
- **SA-0MVAWFYKT002CQ3L** – Stabilise child freshness fingerprint comments (completed)
- **SA-0MSKB6US1009CNHT** – Audit: content-based freshness gate (completed)

### Repository file matches

- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — matched: 0mskb6us1009cnht, 0msn04x2s006onh0, 0mspzdalb000s18p, 0msq026t3009qy2l, 0msq32mf200675ar (+335 more)

## Plan

Decomposed 2026-10-21 (plan skill, Session herdr-1792601836-949358-7572).

Tenet: the parent's strict rule (item data only, zero git calls) re-touches child
reuse, the read-only probe and the ship consumer, so the decomposition keeps every
consumer working against the simplified formula rather than re-designing them.
Code + test migration land in one commit (the repo gate forbids a red commit), so
the test item is created first (test-first creation order) but executed after the
implementation item (blocking edge); its roll is the AC8 "nothing silently dropped"
ledger + mutation-style guards for the new contract.

| # | Child | Type | Priority | Depends on | Summary |
|---|-------|------|----------|-----------|---------|
| 1 | Verify item-data-only audit freshness contract (SA-0MVIDI6EL002E163) | task (test) | high | 2, 4 | Rewrites the per-touched-path/comment invalidation tests to assert the NEW rule (touched-file edits, HEAD moves, comments, lifecycle fields do not invalidate; title/description/Key-Files changes do), adds a zero-git-call guard + exact-payload test, versioned-line legacy fallback tests, and records a migrated-test ledger (parent AC8). |
| 2 | Fingerprint from item data only, v2 line (SA-0MVIDI8E00063OOP) | feature | high | — | Core slice: `_compute_content_fingerprint` hashes `{schema:2, title_hash, description_hash}` with zero git calls; versioned `Audit content fingerprint (v2): ` line; legacy unversioned reports fall back to the time gate; comments param removed at all call sites; TDD test migration in the same commit; docstrings updated. |
| 3 | Remove dead fingerprint git/comment machinery (SA-0MVIDIAAN002UCX6) | task | medium | 2 | Deletes `_compute_path_fingerprints` and `_fetch_item_comments` (grep-verified dead), cleans the children-test scaffolding that patched them; keeps `_resolve_touched_files` (file-scope manifest) and `_resolve_audited_head`. |
| 4 | Ship gates accept versioned fingerprint line (SA-0MVIDICGZ0030DXC) | task | high | — (same release as 2) | Updates the mirrored prefix + `hasContentFingerprint()` in `skill/ship/scripts/check-audit-gate.js` so the release content-freshness fast path keeps working; legacy v1 lines fall back to the local time gate; unit tests extended. |
| 5 | Update freshness-gate documentation (SA-0MVIDIEB8003LFHL) | docs | medium | 2, 3, 4 | Rewrites the freshness-gate sections of `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`, `skill/audit/SKILL.md` and `skill/ship/docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` to the item-data-only / versioned-line / legacy-fallback contract, incl. the one-time legacy re-audit consequence and its pre-flight full-suite cache-gate interaction; stale-reference grep sweep. |

then 5, then 1 (verification last, blocked on 2 + 4). Each item is a vertical slice

**Interview inputs (already settled at intake, not re-asked):** strict rule (a);
title+description only; keep key_files out of the payload (derivative of
description_hash — AC1 permits); versioned line chosen for migration; comments/

## Goal

Prevent the audit runner's Phase-1 code-quality scan from passing non-Python files (YAML, JSON, Markdown, etc.) to ruff as explicit file arguments, eliminating false-positive `invalid-syntax` findings that get auto-created as work items.

## Background / Root cause

On 2026-08-11, an implement self-review audit ran `run_code_quality(files=cq_scope_files)` with the git changed-file list, which included `proxy/config-cheap.yaml` (uncommitted changes at the time). `_run_ruff_check` invoked `ruff check <yaml-file>` — ruff parses YAML as Python and emitted 121 false-positive `invalid-syntax` findings, which `create_epics_for_findings` auto-created as work items under the Quality Improvement epic (LP-0MSJFTRUW0076Z5Y). Those stale items were later marked completed/in_review and drained one-by-one by the herdr downtime audit tier (~59 dispatches in one evening).

The `.ruff.toml` `exclude = ["*.yaml", "*.yml"]` fix (commit 7580063) is **insufficient**: ruff only honors `exclude` for directory scans; explicit file arguments bypass it (verified: `ruff check config-cheap.yaml` with the exclude in place still returns invalid-syntax findings, while `ruff check .` returns `[]`).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `run_ruff` / `_run_ruff_check` filter the `files` list to Python extensions (`.py`, `.pyi`, `.ipynb`) before invoking ruff; non-Python files are skipped and never passed as explicit paths.
2. A regression test asserts ruff is never invoked with a `.yaml`/`.yml` file path when the changed-file list includes one, and that no finding work items are created for non-Python files.
3. Directory-scan behavior (`files=None`) is unchanged.
4. Genuine ruff findings on `.py` files are unaffected (existing tests pass).
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MT2Q10PX0078DEM** – Ruff: exclude YAML & non-Python files additively across all projects (whole-project scan) (completed)
- **SA-0MQPP6TFJ008LU1N** – wl close: add recovery path for done parent with open children (completed)
- **SA-0MRIIQLQI001RQVB** – Refactor command/doc.md for conciseness (completed)

# Chore: install central wl post-pull hook (~/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull)

## Problem

The committed git hooks `.githooks/post-checkout` and `.githooks/post-merge`
(worklog:post-pull-hook:v1) delegate to the **central** per-machine script:

```sh
exec "/home/rgardler/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull" "$@"
```

When `~/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull` is missing, every git
checkout/merge errors with `exec: ...worklog-post-pull: not found` and the
post-pull `wl sync` never runs.

**Current state (verified 2026-10-14):** on this machine the central script
was installed manually on 2026-09-20 as a symlink to the repo's committed
`.githooks/worklog-post-pull`; it resolves and is executable, so
`git checkout`/merge errors no longer occur here. **The remaining gap is
installer support**: `scripts/install_pi.sh` only wires the pre-push hook
into the current project — it never installs the central post-pull script
(no other installer creates `~/.config/pi/.githooks/`). Fresh environments
that rely solely on `install_pi.sh` still regress.

## Users

- Any developer/agent setting up a fresh environment via
  `scripts/install_pi.sh`.
- Any agent running git operations (checkout, merge, pull) inside a project
  that has committed the delegated post-pull hooks.

Example user stories:

- As a developer installing pi-agent infrastructure on a new machine, I want
  `install_pi.sh` to install the central post-pull hook, so that
  `git checkout`/merge doesn't error and worklog syncs after pulls.
- As an agent working in a repo with committed post-pull hooks, I want git
  checkout/merge to run `wl sync` silently, so the worklog stays current
  without hook errors.

## Summary

While shipping LLM-proxy v0.1.19, the ship wrapper was invoked with an unrecognised flag (to read help). It **ran the entire post-release sequence without performing a release**, closing 74 real release-candidate work items with the previous release's reason (`Shipped in v0.1.18`). The real release then found zero candidates and produced an empty changelog. Full incident: llm worklog **LP-0MUEALIM60037F1S**.

## Root cause

1. **No argument validation in `skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js`.** Only `--skip-checks` is wrapper-only; every other flag (including `--help`) is forwarded to `merge-dev-to-main.sh`.
2. **`merge-dev-to-main.sh` treats `-h|--help` as usage and `exit 0`** — so the child succeeds without releasing.
3. **`runReleaseImpl` does not detect the no-op release.** It skips the PR wait (no PR URL), runs a no-op `syncDevWithMain()`, then resolves `version` from `git describe --tags --abbrev=0` — the **previous** tag.
4. **`verifyReleaseMerge(version)` only checks** that the tag exists on `origin` and is an ancestor of `origin/main`. The previous tag already satisfies this, so the guard passes.
5. **`closeWorkItemsAfterRelease(version)` then closes every `stage=in_review` item with the wrong reason.**

## Overlap resolution (duplicate check, Step 4.3)

Steps 1–4 and 5's *close* trigger were fixed by the overlapping, now-completed
work item **SA-0MV0PZYMI004SUFR** ("ship: run-release.js --help runs
post-release steps and closes items against a stale tag") and its children
SA-0MV13B5F8005NT6G (fail-fast CLI), SA-0MV13B5WO008CYXA (newly-created-tag
gate) and SA-0MV13B4YT0093CKT (regression tests). Verified in the current tree:

- `parseReleaseArgs()` + `runRelease()` reject unknown flags (exit 13) and make
  `--help`/`-h` fully inert (usage, exit 0) before the Code Freeze marker or any
  gate runs.
- `snapshotReleaseTags()` / `isNewlyCreatedTag()` gate every post-release step:
  a tag that already existed before the run exits 14 without closing anything.

The remaining, still-unmet gap from the original criteria is **idempotency of
the close sweep**: `closeWorkItemsAfterRelease()` unconditionally re-issues
`wl close --reason "Shipped in v<version>"` for every candidate, so a repeated
post-release run (or an item already annotated for this version by an earlier
sweep) is re-closed and re-annotated — the 99 spurious close comments / 25
double-closed items observed in the incident. This work item now covers that
gap only.

## Desired behaviour / Acceptance Criteria (remaining gap)

- [ ] AC1: `closeWorkItemsAfterRelease(version)` skips any candidate that already carries a close marker for **this** version (`Shipped in v<version>`), with **no** `wl close` and **no** additional comment/annotation for that item; the skipped items are reported in the return value.
- [ ] AC2: The marker match is version-exact — `Shipped in v0.1.1` must not match version `0.1.18` (and vice versa); markers for other versions do not suppress a close.
- [ ] AC3: Reading the existing markers is injectable/fail-safe: an unreadable comment source logs a warning and leaves the existing close behaviour intact (a release is never blocked by the idempotency check); no test touches the live worklog.
- [ ] AC4: Regression tests cover (a) a re-run of the post-release close does not duplicate `wl close` calls or comments, (b) an item carrying another version's marker is still closed, (c) version-exact matching, (d) the unreadable-marker fail-safe path.
- [ ] AC5: Full test suite passes; `skill/ship/SKILL.md` / reference docs describe the idempotency guarantee.

## Key files

- `skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js` — `closeWorkItemsAfterRelease` (marker check), new pure helper for version-exact marker detection.
- `tests/unit/test-close-work-items-after-release.mjs` — regression tests.
- `skill/ship/SKILL.md` / `skill/ship/docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` — documentation.

## Already delivered by SA-0MV0PZYMI004SUFR (not re-implemented here)

- `--help`/`-h` inert; unknown flags rejected non-zero before any post-release step.
- `verifyReleaseMerge` alone is insufficient — a newly-created-tag gate now
  proves *this* run produced the release tag.
- Post-release close/notify/cleanup skipped whenever no new tag was created.

The audit runner's code-quality scan is documented to lint only the work item's changed files (`SA-0MSKB6VWU000RT58` AC1: "the code-quality scan runs only over the git changed-file list … not the full repo"), but it silently falls back to a **whole-repo** scan whenever the changed-file list is empty. For an item whose work is already committed to `dev` (the normal post-merge state, and the state the merge gate integrates to), `git diff --name-only HEAD` + `git status --porcelain` are both empty, so `run_code_quality(files=cq_scope_files or None)` receives `None` and lints the entire repository. Any pre-existing critical/high ruff finding in an unrelated file then blocks Phase 1 of every audit in that repo — a recurrence of the defect class fixed by `SA-0MSG83Z4Z004YH2P` ("EXE001 misclassified as 'high' severity blocks audits on unrelated files") and a contradiction of `SA-0MSKB6VWU000RT58` AC1.

## Repro

1. Work item `LP-0MTYAZFGN003BYQS` (llm) is merged to `origin/dev`; the local checkout is clean at the delivered commit `66ddbe93`.
2. `git diff --name-only HEAD` and `git status --porcelain` are both empty.
3. Run `audit_runner.py issue LP-0MTYAZFGN003BYQS --force`: `_git_changed_files` returns `[]`, so `run_code_quality(files=None)` scans the whole repo.
4. The whole-repo scan returns 4 findings, all outside the item's change set:

`wl sync` overwrites a locally-persisted audit result with an older copy, silently reverting a just-written audit (data loss / audit-record corruption).

## Problem

When a `wl sync` runs after a local audit has been persisted (via the canonical audit persister / `wl audit-set`), the locally written audit text is replaced by an older copy of the audit. The item's other fields (status, stage, `needsProducerReview`, comments, description) are preserved, so the store is left internally inconsistent: the lifecycle reflects the new verdict while the stored audit shows a stale verdict.

Observed 2026-09-26 on `LP-0MSPZUD4G007IYGH` in the LLM project (`/home/rgardler/projects/llm`):

1. The audit runner persisted a new `Ready to close: No` audit at `2026-09-26T13:34:32.382Z`; `wl audit-show` read it back immediately (verified).
2. A herdr-scheduled `wl sync` ran (`.worklog/last-sync-time` advanced to `2026-09-26T13:38:00Z`); afterwards `wl audit-show` returned the **old** `2026-08-15T12:59:45.425Z` `Ready to close: Yes` audit.
3. Re-persisted via `persist_audit.py` at `2026-09-26T13:37:27.757Z`; a further `wl sync` reverted it again.
4. Re-persisted once more at `2026-09-26T13:39:21.882Z` (no sync running); it remained stable while no sync ran.

The item's status/stage (`open`/`plan_complete`) and its comments (including ones added after the new audit) survived each sync — only the audit text reverted.

## Evidence

- The synced export `refs/worklog/remotes/origin/worklog/data:.worklog/worklog-data.jsonl` contains only `workitem` and `comment` records — **no audit field/record at all** (`grep -c '<new-fingerprint>' worklog-data.jsonl` → 0; the `workitem` record keys do not include `audit`).
- Therefore the audit cannot be propagating through the git sync export, yet the old audit reappears after sync — suggesting the audit is not carried by the export and the sync restores/keeps an older audit from another source, or the merge drops local-only audit changes.
- Commands used: `wl audit-show <id> --json`, `persist_audit.py --issue-id <id> --file <report>`, `git for-each-ref refs/worklog/...`, `.worklog/last-sync-time`.
- Worklog prefix: `SA` (this repo). The affected store was `LP` (LLM project).

## Impact

- Audits persisted by the canonical audit runner can be silently reverted, leaving `status`/`stage` inconsistent with the stored audit text (e.g. item demoted to `open`/`plan_complete` while `audit-show` reports a stale `Yes`).
- Operators and orchestrators reading `wl audit-show` can be misled about whether an item is ready to close.
- Concurrent syncs (herdr-scheduled) make the loss deterministic during busy periods, so re-persisting does not reliably fix it.

## Expected behaviour

- A `wl sync` must never downgrade a newer locally-persisted audit to an older one. Merge semantics for audit text should be last-write-wins by audit time (or audits should be excluded from sync-triggered overwrites until pushed).
- If the sync cannot carry audit text in the git export, it must leave the local audit untouched rather than reverting it.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Reproduce in a test: persist audit A (older), then a newer audit B on the same item, run the sync/merge path, and assert `wl audit-show` returns B (not A).
2. The synced worklog export either carries audit records/fields, or the sync merge explicitly preserves the newest local audit (documented decision).
3. A sync that cannot represent audits leaves the local audit unchanged (no revert).
4. Regression fixture uses two audits with distinct `auditedAt` timestamps and the real sync export/import path.
5. Existing worklog sync tests pass.

6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Notes

- Discovered during the audit of `LP-0MSPZUD4G007IYGH` (proxy usage analysis fast/cheap bucketing). Recording it here as instructed by the operator; out of scope for that audit.
- Related: audit persistence ordering contract (comments before persistence), and the audit freshness gate — a reverted audit text also makes the content-fingerprint freshness gate evaluate against the wrong (older) report.

# Intake Brief — `wl sync --if-idle` must never revert an actively-worked claim

## Problem statement

A background `wl sync --if-idle` (herdr-scheduled sync, auto-sync spawn, or the
shared `worklog_sync.py` helper) repeatedly reverted an *actively worked* work
item from `status: in_progress` back to `status: open` / `stage: intake_complete`
while an implement run was in progress — four documented occurrences in a single
run (2026-10-18, SA-0MVDQF3VW002PKCA), each requiring the agent to re-claim the
item between tool calls. This breaks the project invariant *"actively worked
⇒ `in_progress`"* (SA-0MTFTFUIH000UWM9) and lets a sync silently downgrade a
claim, so lifecycle state can no longer be trusted while agents work.

## Users

- **Agents (Map and driven child sessions)** implementing or auditing a work
  item in a background/scheduled-sync environment.
  - *User story:* "As an agent working an item for an hour, I want my claim to
    survive background syncs, so I do not have to re-claim (and re-track
    stage) between every tool call."
- **Producers / operators** watching the board and the audit/ship gates.
  - *User story:* "As a producer, I want `wl show` to reflect who is really
    working on what, so the board and the gate decisions are trustworthy."
- **Orchestrators** (`wl next`, dispatch, downtime worker) that route work by
  `status`/`assignee`/`stage`.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Root cause identified and pinned by a deterministic failing test.** A test
   reproduces the reported symptom (a claimed `in_progress` item is reverted to
   `open`/`intake_complete` by a sync) against current `dev`, and the failure
   discriminates between the two candidate mechanisms below, naming the exact
   code path:
   - **(a) lost update with a fresh stamp** — `wl sync` reads the store, and a
     claim lands in its read→merge→write window; `Database.import()` /
     `upsertItems()` then write the *stale* incoming row and re-stamp it with
     `new Date().toISOString()`, so the downgrade also looks *newer* to every
     later merge (i.e. the mutation lock `WL-0MUV2U9QF002S9J1` is bypassed, or
     the two participants contend on different lock files/stores);
   - **(b) store-resolution divergence** — `.worklog/config.yaml` is tracked in
     git, so every implement worktree contains a `.worklog/` directory with
     config but no store; a `wl` command run with cwd inside the worktree binds
     to a *second* store (its own DB, its own `last-synced-ref` watermark, its
     own push) instead of the main checkout's store, so syncs/snapshots cross
     between two roots and clobber each other.
2. **A sync cannot downgrade a held claim.** After the fix, no sync path (full
   snapshot, delta, `replayRemoteDeltaChain` fallback, `--if-idle` skip logic)
   can reduce a claimed item's `status`/`stage` to a less-active pair while the
   claim is held: immediately after a sync, `wl show` still reports the claimed
   `status`/`stage`, and the claim's `updatedAt`/`activityAt` are preserved
   (not re-stamped). Every such decision (refused, preserved, or a detected
   second store for the same prefix) is recorded in the sync log and the
   `--json` output, so the next field recurrence is diagnosable without source
   archaeology.
3. **Stale claims still release — protection is time-bounded.** Claim
   protection is bounded by a configurable TTL (`sync.claimHoldTtlHours`,
   default 24h; `0` disables the protection), so a genuinely abandoned claim is
   still releasable and a *newer* legitimate transition (close, audit demotion,
   reassignment) still propagates. Newer-wins across roots remains the rule
   outside the TTL window.
4. **One store per repo, enforced.** Whichever mechanism is confirmed, running
   worklog commands from inside an implement/audit worktree must either bind to
   the main checkout's store or fail with a clear, actionable error — it must
   never silently create or sync a second store for the same project prefix.
5. **Regression tests cover claims and existing sync guarantees.**
   `tests/cli/sync-vs-mutation.test.ts` gains claim-specific cases (status-only
   claim, status+stage claim, assignee-only hold), and the existing
   sync guarantees stay green: `sync-regression-guard.test.ts`,
   `sync-delta-{pull,push,delete,fallback}.test.ts`,
   `sync-assignee-clear.test.ts`, `sync-audit-newest-wins.test.ts`,
   `sync-integration-convergence.test.ts`.
6. **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including
   code comments, `CLI.md`/`DATA_SYNCING.md` (ContextHub) and the shared
   `docs/dev/worklog-sync.md` + `skill/shared/worklog_sync.py` docstring here.
7. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **Change site is the ContextHub repo** (`~/projects/ContextHub`, prefix `WL`),
  the canonical source of the `wl` CLI; `/usr/local/lib/node_modules/worklog`
  is a symlink to it, so no reinstall step is needed after a build. This SA item
  tracks the work and carries the commit record (precedent: SA-0MUJNFF3K009BF03
  was implemented in ContextHub).
- **`--if-idle` semantics unchanged**: skip (exit 0, `skipped: true`) when
  another sync holds the lock; do not turn it into a blocking wait and do not
  weaken the lock-storm protection.
- **No resurrection regressions**: the delete protections
  (SA-0MSKZ30SK007K9TO), the audit newest-wins rule (SA-0MUJNFF3K009BF03), the
  cross-project prefix filter (SA-0MSC0BM1V0032UYT) and the author-identity
  gate (SA-0MVB57M02008QPJS) must keep their current behaviour.
- **Fixed-but-older data must still lose**: an older snapshot may still lose to
  a newer legitimate write; the fix may not freeze any fieldset.
- **Claim protection is not "last writer wins on status"**: it must be a
  monotonic guard (never downgrade a *held* claim), not an unconditional local
  precedence.
- **No ad-hoc full-suite runs** during implementation (test-execution policy);
  the changed-scope gate and the `/skill:test` route are the only sanctioned
  runs.

## Existing state

- Installed CLI: `worklog@1.0.22` (ContextHub `dev`); `wl` → ContextHub
  `dist/cli.js`.
- **Regression guard is stage-blind below `idea`.** `isRegressionDefault()`
  (`src/sync.ts`) treats only `status: open` and `stage: idea` as regression
  defaults, so a downgrade `stage: in_progress → intake_complete` is a
  *non-default → non-default* change and is resolved by timestamp rather than
  refused. `status: open` against a local `in_progress` *is* guarded, so the
  reported pair (`open` + `intake_complete`) implies the write path, not only
  the merge path.
- **`Database.import()` re-stamps stale rows as new.** In
  `packages/shared/src/database.ts`, `import()` clears all items then re-inserts
  the merged set, and for any item whose tracked fields differ from the
  snapshot it stamps `updatedAt = new Date().toISOString()`. A stale row that
  slipped into the merged set therefore *becomes* the newest row — every later
  merge then honours it. `upsertItems()` (delta path) has the same re-stamp
  behaviour for changed items.
- **The general lost-update race was already fixed** by
  `WL-0MUV2U9QF002S9J1` / CG-0MUUFGXFX004O2X7 (ContextHub commit `ed0acc60`,
  2026-10-05): all mutating commands (`update`, `create`, `close`, `comment`,
  `reviewed`, `dep`, `delete`, `audit-*`, …) take the store mutation lock, and
  `tests/cli/sync-vs-mutation.test.ts` parks a sync inside `git fetch` to prove
  it. The four recurrences reported here (2026-10-18) happened **after** that
  fix, so the residual mechanism is claim-specific or store-scoped, and must be
  identified rather than assumed.
- **Two stores are possible per repo.** `.worklog/config.yaml` is tracked
  (`.gitignore` re-includes it), so each implement worktree materialises a
  `.worklog/` directory that `wl`'s cwd-chain resolution treats as the store
  root; the lock path is derived from the data path, so two such roots contend
  on *different* locks and hold *different* `last-synced-ref` watermarks.
  Sibling symptom already filed: SA-0MVK2G09X00239YL (*implement.py finish
  reports status changes that the main worklog store does not show*).
- Observed evidence: SA-0MVDQF3VW002PKCA comment `2026-10-18T17:13:29.348Z`
  ("4th recurrence"), with the item's state reverting mid-run
  (`implement` started 16:04 on the same item).

## Desired change

A claimed item stays claimed across background syncs: the sync path either
refuses to write a downgrade for a held claim (monotonic guard, TTL-bounded)
or never sees a competing store in the first place (single-store resolution),
depending on the mechanism the reproduction test proves. Lifecycle state
written by an agent remains authoritative until the agent itself moves it.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `~/projects/ContextHub/src/commands/sync.ts` — pull → merge → persist → push
  pipeline; where a monotonic claim guard and diagnostics belong.
- `~/projects/ContextHub/src/sync.ts` — `mergeWorkItems`,
  `isRegressionDefault`/`isValueRegression`, `mergeDifferentTimestampItems`
  (stage ordering, not just `idea`/`open`).
- `~/projects/ContextHub/packages/shared/src/database.ts` — `import()` /
  `upsertItems()` stale-row re-stamp guard (compare incoming `updatedAt`).
- `~/projects/ContextHub/src/mutation-lock.ts`, `src/file-lock.ts` — lock
  identity derived from the data path (hypothesis (a) bypass surface).
- `~/projects/ContextHub/src/worklog-paths.ts` (+ `src/config.ts`) — store
  discovery/`.worklog` resolution from a worktree cwd (hypothesis (b)).
- `~/projects/ContextHub/tests/cli/sync-vs-mutation.test.ts` — deterministic
  window-widening harness to extend with claim cases.
- `~/projects/ContextHub/tests/cli/sync-regression-guard.test.ts` — stage
  ordering expectations.
- `~/projects/SorraAgents/docs/dev/worklog-sync.md`,
  `skill/shared/worklog_sync.py` — document claim preservation + single-store
  rule for agents.

## Related work

| ID | Title | Status | Relationship |
|----|-------|--------|--------------|
| SA-0MVDQF3VW002PKCA | User-visible progress feedback in the Pi agent interface during long-running waits | completed | Discovery source: the 4 recurrences were recorded while implementing this item |
| WL-0MUV2U9QF002S9J1 (CG-0MUUFGXFX004O2X7) | Serialise mutating commands on store lock | completed | Landed the general lost-update fix (commit `ed0acc60`); recurrences post-date it — this item covers the residual claim case |
| SA-0MUJNFF3K009BF03 | `wl sync` reverts locally-persisted audit results to a stale older audit | completed | Same family: destructive `import()` vs. newer local state; its newest-wins rule must not regress |
| SA-0MSAK2W0F0027ZP7 | `wl sync` serialization | completed | Introduced/verified the sync file lock (`--if-idle` depends on it) |
| SA-0MVK2G09X00239YL | `implement.py finish` reports status changes that the main worklog store does not show | open | Probable sibling symptom of the two-store hypothesis |
| SA-0MTFTFUIH000UWM9 | Always mark items as `in_progress` while an agent is working on them | completed | The invariant this bug violates |
| SA-0MSKZ30SK007K9TO | Unattributed deletes must not win by recency | completed | Delete-side protection that must not regress |
| SA-0MSC0BM1V0032UYT | ContextHub (WL-) items re-contaminated the SorraAgents worklog | completed | Cross-project prefix guard that must not regress |

Automated related-work report (`find-related`, recorded for traceability):

- SA-0MR12G1NH0097Z59 — *Clarify stage vs status lifecycle in AGENTS.md and implement skill* (completed) — stage/status semantics raised by this bug.
- SA-0MQWVU3A6007F38B — *Intake skill auto-complete leaves work-item as `in_progress` instead of `open`* (completed) — adjacent lifecycle-drift defect.
- SA-0MRGVN9XM003LNQ7 — *Close work items when shipping* (completed) — terminal-transition semantics that the TTL guard must not break.
- Repository matches: `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`, `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`, `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` (agent-facing callers of `wl`/sync).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — fixing the symptom in the wrong layer.** A blanket "local claim
  always wins" rule would resurrect abandoned claims forever and block
  legitimate demotions; the TTL bound (AC3) is the mitigation.
- **Risk — the reproduction is timing-dependent.** Mitigation: reuse the
  `sync-vs-mutation.test.ts` `git`-shim parking technique, which widens the
  read→write window deterministically; do not ship a sleep-based test.
- **Risk — two-store divergence is an environment/instruction bug, not a sync
  bug.** If hypothesis (b) is confirmed, the code fix may be small (refuse or
  re-root) but the agent-facing rule (always pass
  `--worklog-dir <main>/.worklog`) needs to be enforced/documented; both are in
  scope under AC4/AC7.
- **Risk — `updatedAt` semantics are load-bearing** for audits
  (`isAuditFresh`), sorting and demotion. Any change to stamping must be
  verified against `sync-audit-newest-wins`, `dirty-tracking` and
  `grouping` expectations.
- **Assumption:** the guarded claim is identified by `status: in_progress`
  (and/or a non-empty `assignee`) with a `updatedAt`/`activityAt` inside the
  TTL; `stage` alone is not a claim.
- **Assumption:** default TTL 24h with `sync.claimHoldTtlHours: 0` to disable —
  chosen so an 8-hour drive run is always protected while a day-old abandoned
  claim can still be released; adjust in planning if the producer prefers.
- **Scope-creep (explicitly out of scope):** redesigning the
  claim/assignee-hold model (SA-0MVA79DNT001HQBB), replacing the delta sync
  format, and the Pi-client side of SA-0MVK2G09X00239YL — record those as
  linked work items rather than expanding this fix.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No producer interview round was required: the seed context (discovery comment
plus the two sibling work items) already defined the symptom, and the remaining
uncertainty is a *technical* discrimination that must be settled by a
reproduction test, not by producer preference. Research below is recorded with
evidence so the implementer does not repeat it.

- **Q:** Is this a duplicate of the already-fixed `wl sync` lost-update race?
  — **Answer (Map, research):** No, and not a duplicate item either. The
  general race (`wl update`/`comment add`/`audit-set` vs sync) was fixed by
  `WL-0MUV2U9QF002S9J1` (commit `ed0acc60`, 2026-10-05; regression suite
  `tests/cli/sync-vs-mutation.test.ts`), yet the reported reverts occurred
  2026-10-18. Sources: `~/projects/ContextHub/src/mutation-lock.ts` header,
  `git log -- src/mutation-lock.ts`, SA-0MVDQF3VW002PKCA comments.

- **Q:** Could the merge layer alone explain `open` + `intake_complete`?
  — **Answer (Map, research):** Partly, not fully.
  `isRegressionDefault()` (`~/projects/ContextHub/src/sync.ts`) only treats
  `status: open` and `stage: idea` as regression defaults, so
  `stage: in_progress → intake_complete` is resolved by timestamp instead of
  being refused (a stage-ordering gap), while `status: open` *is* refused when
  the remote is the stale side. Getting the *pair* requires a write path that
  installs the stale row locally.

- **Q:** Which write path can install a stale row *and* make it look new?
  — **Answer (Map, research):** `Database.import()` and `upsertItems()`
  (`~/projects/ContextHub/packages/shared/src/database.ts`) re-stamp any
  semantically-changed incoming row with `updatedAt = new Date().toISOString()`
  after `clearWorkItems()`. A stale row admitted into the merged set therefore
  wins from then on. This is hypothesis (a).

- **Q:** Is there a plausible second root cause worth testing?
  — **Answer (Map, research):** Yes — hypothesis (b): `.worklog/config.yaml` is
  tracked (`.gitignore` re-includes it, verified with `git ls-files .worklog`),
  so implement worktrees get a `.worklog/` directory with no store; `wl`'s
  cwd-chain resolution binds there, and the mutation lock plus the
  `last-synced-ref` watermark are both derived from the data path, so two roots
  do not contend. Sibling symptom already filed as SA-0MVK2G09X00239YL.

- **Q:** Does claim protection risk freezing a genuinely abandoned claim?
  — **Answer (Map, decision):** Bounded by the TTL in AC3 (default 24h,
  `sync.claimHoldTtlHours: 0` disables). Assumption recorded above for planning.

- **Q:** Where should the fix land, and how is it tracked from an `SA` item?
  — **Answer (Map, research):** In the ContextHub repo (`WL` prefix), which is
  the canonical `wl` source and the symlink target of the installed package;
  precedent SA-0MUJNFF3K009BF03. This `SA` item carries the brief, the
  implementation comments, and the commit record.

## Goal

Refine the audit stage's acceptance of full-suite evidence: matching-git-state GREEN cached entries are accepted **without a practical time bound** (code identity is already guaranteed by the git-state key), so audit re-runs never occur purely because evidence is old. Red entries keep the existing 5-minute failed-run expiry.

## Problem (discovered-from:SA-0MVECQUGF0064U81)

SA-0MVECQUGF0064U81 shipped `AUDIT_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS = 24h` as the audit's acceptance window. The operator's challenge is valid: the full suite was proven green by the dev-push gate at the pushed commit; the cache key is the byte-identical git state, so the wall clock adds nothing about the CODE. Environment drift (deps/infra/host state) is the only thing a time bound hedges, and it is already caught fresh at the next dev-push and by the enforced ship release gate (AC4) before anything ships. A 24h expiry therefore causes needless F3 full-suite re-runs (slot contention) for re-audits, backlogs and HEAD-drifted audits with no safety gain.

## Requirements

1. Replace the 24h audit acceptance with a no-practical-bound semantics for GREEN entries (e.g. an explicitly documented large `AUDIT_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS`, or an explicit green-never-expires mode in the audit's lookup); non-zero-exit entries remain capped at the 5-minute failed-run TTL (`lookup()` already applies `min(ttl, FAILED_RUN_TTL_SECONDS)`).
2. Pin the semantics with tests: a green entry backdated well beyond 24h (e.g. 120 days) still classifies GREEN; a green entry beyond the generic 2h TTL is NOT a miss; a failed entry still expires at 5 minutes.
3. Update skill/audit/SKILL.md and docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md (remove the "24h acceptance window" language).
4. F3 (auto-execute on genuine miss) and F4 (never-block) behaviour unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria (testable)

- AC1: A green full-suite entry backdated 120 days at a matching git state classifies as AUTO-VERIFIED GREEN (no F3 execution).
- AC2: A failed (non-zero) entry still expires after the 5-minute TTL and is never accepted as evidence.
- AC3: Audit docs no longer describe a time-based acceptance window for green entries; they state green evidence at a matching git state is accepted without a practical time bound (grep-verifiable).
- AC4: All tests pass via the test skill (changed-scope and the audit test group); changes committed and pushed to dev.

## Goal

Make the changed-scope test gate run the **union of all matching skill groups**, not a single arbitrary pick, and align the two selectors (implement.py `run_tests` and `run_tests.py --scope changed`) on the same semantics.

## Problem (discovered-from:SA-0MVECQUGF0064U81)

`select_group_from_changed_files` returns the single group with the fewest commands; when multiple groups match with equal command counts, `min(matching, key=matching.get)` returns an arbitrary one (insertion order). A cross-skill change — e.g. touching `skill/implement/**`, `skill/test/**` and `skill/audit/**` simultaneously, exactly like SA-0MVECQUGF0064U81 — therefore gate-tests only ONE of the affected skill suites pre-commit, deferring the rest to the push-time full gate (and the import-graph selector cannot cover them: `map_changed_to_tests` only scans root `tests/`/`test/` dirs, not skill-group test dirs). The run_tests.py CLI's `--scope changed` uses a different (file-level) selector than implement.py's group-first selector, so the two agree only by accident.

## Requirements

1. A changed set matching N groups (e.g. implement + test + audit) runs the commands of ALL N groups exactly once (deduplicated), with each suite's cache key/type metadata preserved (`group:<name>`).
2. Matching-group selection becomes deterministic and documented (union by paths; no arbitrary single pick). When no group matches, behaviour falls back to the existing file-level selector / full suite unchanged.
3. implement.py `run_tests(scope="changed")` and `run_tests.py --scope changed` converge on the same group-union semantics (single source of truth for group selection).
4. Per-command timeouts account for N groups (a multi-group run must not blow the 600s default); cache entries remain distinct per group.

## Acceptance Criteria (testable)

- AC1: A change touching `skill/implement/**`, `skill/test/**` and `skill/audit/**` invokes all three groups' suite commands in a `--scope changed` run.
- AC2: A group matching multiple changed files runs once (no duplicate commands).
- AC3: The CLI (`run_tests.py --scope changed`) and `implement.py` finish select the same command set for the same changed set (convergence test).
- AC4: No group match → existing fallback behaviour unchanged (file-level selection, then full).
- AC5: All tests pass via the test skill; changes committed and pushed to dev.

# Audit wall-clock reduction: diagnose and fix why audits take hours

## Problem statement

Item-level audits routinely take hours (measured: 4.25h for a 10-child parent) and
even single-item audits exceed 30 minutes, to the point where operators avoid
running them and release gates stall. Instrumented data from every audit log on
this host shows the cost is not one slow operation but a **long chain of slow,
serial LLM calls against a 2-slot local proxy, oversubscribed by a concurrency
ceiling of 6**, with roughly **18% of total call time producing no usable result**
(timeouts and JSON re-asks).

## Users

- **Release producer** — blocked at the `ship` audit gate, waiting hours for a re-audit.
- **Implementation agent** — cannot complete the implement skill's self-review audit within a session budget.
- **Operator** — avoids auditing, so `in_review` items accumulate unreviewed.

Example user stories:

- As a release producer, I want a single-item audit to finish in **≤ 10 minutes** on a healthy proxy so the `dev`→`main` gate is not a multi-hour stall.
- As an implementation agent, I want a parent audit with 10 children to finish in **≤ 30 minutes** so it fits one session and aborts less often.
- As an operator, I want a **reproducible measurement** of audit wall-clock so I can verify a change actually helped instead of guessing.

## Diagnosis — why audits are slow (measured)

Source: `Per-call timing:` lines from `~/.audit_debug/*/*.log`
(465 logs, 491 distinct work items, **1,637 instrumented LLM calls, 140.8h total**).
Reproduce with the script specified in AC1.

### Call-time distribution by phase

| Context | calls | total | p50 | p90 | max |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `parent` (Phase 1 parent screen) | 450 | **48.3h** | 220s | 954s | 2,705s |
| `child` (Phase 1 child screen) | 412 | **38.1h** | 227s | 633s | 1,572s |
| `verdict_reask` (JSON-contract retry) | 121 | **18.7h** | 461s | 1,466s | 2,372s |
| `phase2_deep` | 285 | 16.0h | 102s | 513s | 1,800s |
| `phase2_child` | 316 | 15.8h | 101s | 529s | 1,775s |
| `false-positive-screen` | 53 | 3.9h | 168s | 600s | 1,200s |

Median call **158s**; 76% of calls ≥ 60s; 35% ≥ 300s.

### Root causes, ranked by measured cost

1. **Phase 1 screening is 62% of all call time (86.4h).** It runs as parent
   screen → N child screens, each a fresh full-prompt session, and averages
   220–227s per call for what is structurally *screening*, not deep analysis.
2. **Concurrency ceiling (6) is 3× the proxy's real capacity (2 slots).**
   `GET /llama/local/status` reports `total_slots: 2`, `available_slots: 0`.
   Six concurrent `pi` sessions queue behind two slots; the queue wait is
   charged against each call's own timeout budget, inflating p90 latency.
3. **~25h of pure timeout waste.** Calls landing exactly on a budget:
   **96 at 600s** (child-screen budget), **13 at 1,800s**, **86 at 90s**.
   Each returns a `partial` fallback that does no work and forces a later re-run.
4. **18.7h of JSON-contract re-asks.** 121 `verdict_reask` calls exist only
   because the first response was not parseable JSON — and the re-ask itself
   has p50 461s, *slower* than the call it retries.
5. **No reuse across the pipeline.** Every phase re-sends its own large prompt;
   a single edited description or touched file invalidates the content
   fingerprint and discards all prior screening work.

### Where the levers are

| Lever | Measured/expected saving | Status in code |
|---|---|---|
| Size concurrency to real slot capacity | removes queue-induced inflation + most 600s/1,800s timeout waste | ceiling hardcoded default 6 (`process_semaphore.py`); slot-status query exists but only used for *child* ceiling |
| Eliminate JSON re-asks | up to 18.7h of 140.8h | `_reask_json_array_once` exists as the fallback; parse robustness not hardened |
| Batch Phase 1 parent+children into one call | collapses N+1 screens to ~1 | `--batch-phase2` exists for Phase 2 only, off by default |
| Route Phase 1 to a fast model | Phase 1 is 62% of time, low-reasoning work | `phase1_model` plumbing exists but **no CLI/env surface**; tiered-model item was demoted |
| Adaptive timeout + degrade early | converts 25h of dead time into fast partials | fixed 600s/1,800s budgets |

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Reproducible measurement harness committed.** A script (e.g. `scripts/measure_audit_performance.py`) parses `Per-call timing:` lines from `~/.audit_debug/` and prints the per-context table above (calls, total, p50, p90, max, and count-at-budget). Running it on this host reproduces the baseline numbers in this brief within expected variance, and it is covered by a unit test with a fixture corpus.
- **Baseline is recorded and a target is set.** The measured baseline (1,637 calls / 140.8h / 62% Phase 1 / 18% wasted) is committed to `docs/dev/` and a small-item audit wall-clock target of **≤ 10 minutes** (healthy proxy, no concurrent audits) is stated and used as the regression gate.
- **Concurrency ceiling is sized to real capacity.** The audit runner derives its parallel-call ceiling from the live slot status (`available_slots` / `total_slots`) with a safe floor, never exceeding that capacity, and falls back to the static ceiling when the query fails. Unit tests prove: 2-slot proxy ⇒ ceiling ≤ 2; failed query ⇒ configured fallback; explicit `AUDIT_MAX_CONCURRENCY` remains authoritative.
- **JSON-contract re-asks are substantially eliminated.** Parse robustness is hardened (strict schema instruction, tolerant extraction, single retry only on genuine failures) and a regression test proves a well-formed model response is never re-asked. Measured `verdict_reask` count drops to ≤ 2% of calls in a re-measurement on the same corpus.
- **Phase 1 call count is reduced.** Parent + child Phase 1 screening is batched and/or routed to a faster model so a 10-child parent issues materially fewer serial Phase 1 calls; a test proves the call count for a 10-child parent is reduced versus the current N+1 structure, with no change to `met`/`unmet`/`partial`/`adjusted` verdict semantics or the ready-to-close gate.
- **Post-change measurement demonstrates the reduction.** Re-running the AC1 harness after implementation shows overall audit LLM wall-clock reduced by **≥ 50%** on a representative audit, with no increase in `partial`-fallback rate and no relaxation of any closure criterion.
- **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including code comments, `skill/audit/SKILL.md`, the audit skill reference, and `docs/dev/audit-phase2-measured-report.md` (or a superseding report).
- **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Verdict semantics are frozen:** no change may relax the ready-to-close gate;
  a `partial` fallback must never degrade to `met`. Correctness outranks speed.
- **Do not simply raise timeouts.** The historical 900→1200→1800s bumps masked
  the inefficiency; this work reduces actual work, not the ceiling.
- Only **2 local proxy slots** exist — any parallel design must be safe below
  saturation, and must not starve interactive `pi` sessions.
- The runner is a `[READ-ONLY AUDIT]` except the already-documented persistence,
  lifecycle, and ruff-remediation exceptions — no new state mutations.
- Changes land on `dev` only; full suite must be green at the push gate.

## Existing state

- Prior epics `SA-0MSADWWH3003N82D` (Phase 2 perf, P1–P6) and P7
  (`SA-0MSF3RXU8005CFGD`) are **complete** and moved the bottleneck from Phase 2
  to Phase 1; that is now confirmed by measurement (§Diagnosis).
- Existing reports: `docs/dev/audit-phase2-performance-evaluation.md`,
  `docs/dev/audit-phase1-performance-evaluation.md`,
  `docs/dev/audit-phase2-measured-report.md`.
- Existing levers already in code but not effective by default: `--batch-phase2`,
  `phase1_model` plumbing, child-verdict reuse, content fingerprint gate,
  per-phase checkpoints.
- Related open items: `SA-0MSRVI17W004U9G0` (simplify audit freshness) and
  `SA-0MUSZJRB9006ZCHE` (queue/concurrency tuning, done but ceiling remains 6).

## Desired change

A measurable, repeatable audit performance programme: (1) lock in the harness and
baseline, (2) size concurrency to real slot capacity, (3) eliminate JSON re-asks,
(4) collapse Phase 1 call count via batching and/or a fast Phase 1 model, and
(5) re-measure to prove ≥ 50% wall-clock reduction — decomposed into child work
items during the plan stage.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — Phase 1 screening, `_call_pi`, timeout
  and parallelism resolution, `_reask_json_array_once`, batch-mode gates.
- `skill/shared/process_semaphore.py` — concurrency ceiling default (6).
- `skill/audit/scripts/scan.py` — slot-status query reused for the ceiling.
- `scripts/measure_audit_performance.py` — new measurement harness (AC1).
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_concurrency.py` — ceiling-from-slots tests.
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_json_contract_reask.py` — re-ask elimination tests.
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_phase1.py` — Phase 1 call-count tests.
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md`, `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`,
  `docs/dev/audit-phase2-measured-report.md` — documentation.

## Related work

- `SA-0MSK9IOEF007PP5S` — **Audit skill: reduce audit wall-clock time (audits far too slow)** (completed). This is the closest prior attempt and shares the same problem statement. It delivered the content freshness gate, gated child cascade, and scoped code-quality scan — **partial overlap**. This item is deliberately scoped to the *residual* drivers those levers did not remove (Phase 1 = 62% of call time, concurrency ceiling 6 vs 2 real slots, JSON re-asks, ~25h of timeout waste), plus the measurement harness needed to prove any future change is real. It does not re-do the freshness/cascade/scoping work.
- `SA-0MSADWWH3003N82D` — Audit skill Phase 2 performance evaluation and improvement (complete).
- `SA-0MSF3RXU8005CFGD` — Phase 1 performance treatment (P7) (complete).
- `SA-0MUSZJRB9006ZCHE` — audit queue timeout / concurrency ceiling tuning (complete; ceiling still 6).
- `SA-0MSRVI17W004U9G0` — simplify audit freshness invalidation (open).
- `SA-0MU32H6KY0021SJL` — audit reliability RCA (reliability, not latency).
- Docs: `docs/dev/audit-phase1-performance-evaluation.md`,
  `docs/dev/audit-phase2-performance-evaluation.md`,
  `docs/dev/audit-phase2-measured-report.md`, `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`.

## Duplicate-work check

Searched `audit`, `speed up`, `Phase 2`, and all prior Phase 1/2 performance items.
One partial overlap found (`SA-0MSK9IOEF007PP5S`, completed) — its delivered ACs
(freshness gate, child-cascade opt-in, scoped code-quality scan) are **not** the
same as this item's ACs, and re-measurement shows the problem persists. Scope
rewritten to the residual gaps only; recorded above under Related work. One
accidental duplicate created during this intake (`SA-0MVF1GHVX008Q66T`) was
closed as a duplicate of this item.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** the logged `Per-call timing` corpus is representative; it is
  derived from this host's real audit history (491 items) and is the only
  latency evidence available.
- **Risk (quality):** batching Phase 1 into fewer, larger calls could reduce
  verdict quality — mitigated by keeping per-AC verdict semantics and comparing
  verdict output before/after on a fixed item set.
- **Risk (contention):** a parallel design sized to slots could still contend
  with interactive sessions — mitigated by a floor of 1 and never exceeding
  `available_slots`.
- **Risk (scope creep):** adjacency to freshness simplification
  (`SA-0MSRVI17W004U9G0`) and the merge-gate work — those stay separate items;
  this epic links rather than absorbs them.
- **Risk (measurement):** historical numbers were taken under concurrent audit
  load; targets must be re-measured clean-room for a fair comparison.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q:** Is the complaint about *all* audits or a specific class (single-item vs
  multi-child parent)?
  **Answer (operator, seed prompt):** "Audits take far too long" — general.
  Diagnosis shows both are affected: single-item ~10–30 min, 10-child parent
  4.25h. Scope therefore covers both, with the parent case as the primary target.
  Source: seed prompt `/intake` request; evidence: per-context table above.

- **Q:** Should the fix raise timeouts or reduce actual work?
  **Answer (derived from prior art):** Reduce actual work. Prior bumps
  (900→1200→1800s) are documented as masking inefficiency
  (`docs/dev/audit-phase2-performance-evaluation.md` §1). Source: repo docs.

- **Q:** Is switching off the local proxy (to a remote model) acceptable?
  **Answer (OPEN QUESTION — producer decision):** assumed *permitted but not
  required*; the plan prefers fast/local routing and treats remote routing
  (e.g. `deepseek-v4-flash`) as an option to confirm. Source: this intake;
  needs producer confirmation at plan review.

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-21T15:12:22Z — plan skill decomposed this epic into 7 children (1 pre-existing task + 6 new
  features) and wired 11 dependency edges in test-first ordering (harness/baseline →
  concurrency ceiling + JSON re-asks + child-screen budget → Phase 1 call count →
  post-change verification → documentation). Parent AC markers were normalised from
  `1.` numbering to `- ` bullets and unwrapped to single lines so the shared
  tree-coverage review can machine-check parent→child AC coverage; each child carries
  a "Parent ACn traceability" bullet. Coverage review: 100% (action `proceed`).

- 2026-10-23T10:41:00Z — plan re-run (idempotent). Post-change measurement
  `SA-0MVI6VVC00029XO4` reported the AC6 gate **not met** and raised
  `SA-0MVJ3Q662006RDJR` (Parent Phase-1 screen: budget, batching and JSON
  robustness) as the uncovered `+1` of the N+1 Phase 1 structure. That child was
  planned (`plan_complete`, effort **Small** / risk **Medium**, expected 15.08h,
  WBS recorded), the 8-child tree was re-verified (all 8 parent ACs owned,
  coverage action `proceed`), and no duplicate children were created. Parent
  advanced to `plan_complete`; the epic stays open until the new child lands and
  AC6 is re-measured.

# Audit runner: parent-persisted child audits demote snapshot-exempt children

**Discovered-from:** WL-0MVFNMSRW002FI6B (ContextHub) — canonicalised here because this repository owns the audit skill.
**Issue type:** bug · **Priority:** high · **Recurrence of:** SA-0MUJAPC680078396 (completed) and SA-0MSGMR7CX00588TZ (completed)
**RCA:** `docs/dev/audit-child-demotion-rca.md`

## Problem statement

A parent audit running in **separate-process child mode** (`--no-child-in-main-slot`) demoted **all 11** of its children from `completed`/`in_review` to `open`/`blocked` at `plan_complete`, at the exact timestamps their child audits were persisted. F1 and F8 (the two dependency-free children) were set to `open`; the other nine cascaded to `blocked` through the dependency chain. The parent's own verdict then read `Ready to close: No` with the sole blocker being those now-`plan_complete` children, even though all six of its own acceptance criteria were `met`/`adjusted`.

This is the side-effect demotion that SA-0MUJAPC680078396 explicitly forbids and that SA-0MSGMR7CX00588TZ was meant to prevent ('infra-fallback verdicts must never demote').

## Root cause (proven)

`_persist_child_audit()` persists child audits through `persist_audit.py`, which calls:

    wl audit-set <child> --ready-to-close no

and `wl audit-set` with a negative verdict calls `db.revertToPlanComplete(child)` (`src/commands/audit-result.ts:207-214`; `packages/shared` `database.revertToPlanComplete`), which unconditionally rewrites `completed`/`in_review` → `open`/`plan_complete`.

Two invariants are therefore bypassed:

1. **The audited item's lifecycle guards.** `ac_fallback_used` (SA-0MSGMR7CX00588TZ) and `_cascade_suppress_demotion` (SA-0MUJAPC680078396) live in `_apply_terminal_lifecycle` for the *item under audit*. `persist_audit` → `audit-set` is a skill-unaware primitive and consults neither.
2. **The child-exemption snapshot.** `_child_is_exempt` is only consulted by the runner's own closure checks, not by `audit-set`.

Measured: 8 of 11 children were persisted with `readyToClose=false` (`wl audit-show --json`) and every one was reverted; the 3 with `true` were not. Dependency cascade then produced the 9 `blocked` states.

**Aggravating factor.** Those child verdicts were infra-fallback-tainted: `AUDIT_RELIABILITY_SUMMARY calls=27 parse_ok=20 parse_failed=7 timeouts=7`, with 5 of 11 child Phase-1 screens landing exactly on the 600 s `AUDIT_CHILD_SCREEN_TIMEOUT` cap. Per SA-0MSGMR7CX00588TZ an infra-fallback 'No' is not an explicit model assessment and must take the **restore** path — but `audit-set` has no notion of fallback provenance, so tainted verdicts demote.

**Open sub-question (to confirm in this item).** The parent's closure reported those children as blocking even though they were `in_review` at audit start and `_capture_exempt_children_snapshot` should have exempted them. `all_children_reviewed` honours `snapshot_exempt` (audit_runner.py ~5633) but the report's `not_reviewed` text path (~5759) does **not**, so text and verdict can disagree. Determine whether the snapshot was empty (children already demoted pre-snapshot), lost, or simply not applied to the text path.

## User stories

- **Audit operator** — As an operator, I want a parent audit to leave the lifecycle of children that were `in_review` at audit start untouched, so a read-only run never pushes completed work back into the actionable queue.
- **Release manager** — As a release manager, I want `blocked` never to cascade through a dependency chain as a side effect of an audit, so a release gate cannot be stalled by an audit artefact.
- **Maintainer** — As a maintainer, I want infra-fallback child verdicts to be recorded as `partial` diagnostics, never as lifecycle-changing 'No's.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A child audit persisted by a parent run (both child-audit modes) **cannot** change a child's status/stage when the child was `completed`/`in_review` at audit start: `_persist_child_audit`/`persist_audit` either writes the audit without the `audit-set` reversion side effect, or the runner restores the captured pre-audit status/stage immediately after persisting.
2. Infra-fallback-tainted child verdicts (parse failure, timeout, provider error, concurrency limit) never demote any item — the same rule SA-0MSGMR7CX00588TZ applies to the audited item now applies to children persisted by a parent.
3. No `blocked` status may be introduced on any work item as a side effect of an audit run; verified by a regression test asserting the full child set's status/stage is byte-identical before and after a parent audit.
4. The parent's closure decision and its report text use the **same** exemption source: `not_reviewed` (~5759) honours `snapshot_exempt`, so a parent whose children were all `in_review` at audit start reports `Ready to close: Yes` when its own ACs pass.
5. A regression test covers the observed scenario end to end (parent + N children, all `in_review`, child verdicts `No` and tainted): children end `completed`/`in_review`, parent verdict `Yes`, no `blocked`.
6. `skill/audit/tests/` passes, including the new tests.

## Evidence

ContextHub run log: `~/.audit_debug/ContextHub/audit-WL-0MVFNMSRW002FI6B-2nd-20261021-102346.log` (9312 s; `AUDIT_RELIABILITY_SUMMARY calls=27 parse_ok=20 parse_failed=7 timeouts=7`). Child `readyToClose` values and the pre/post lifecycle states are reproducible from the child items under `WL-0MVFNMSRW002FI6B`.
